# OpenAI API Platform Provider

Terraform provider for OpenAI API Platform administration and beta project webhook APIs.

## Webhook beta status

Webhook endpoint resources and data sources are beta. Their API and Terraform
schema may change before general availability. Organization-level webhook
management is not part of this API surface.

## Authentication

The provider accepts separate credentials for its two API audiences:

| Terraform operations | Provider attribute | Environment variable | Required authority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Organization administration, including every `openai_project*` resource and data source | `admin_api_key` | `OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY` | [OpenAI Admin API key](https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/admin-keys) |
| Beta project webhook resources and data sources | `api_key` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Project API key with `api.webhooks.read`; full lifecycle management also requires `api.webhooks.write` and project-owner authority |

Set one or both credentials according to the resources in your configuration:

```sh
export OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY="<your-admin-api-key>"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="<your-project-api-key>"
```

Credentials are routed only to their matching audience. The provider does not
inspect a key to infer its audience and never retries an operation with the
other credential. If a required credential is absent, the affected resource or
data source reports which provider attribute or environment variable to set. If
a credential is placed in the wrong attribute, it is sent only to that
attribute's API audience and the OpenAI API rejects the request.

The `project` provider attribute, or `OPENAI_PROJECT_ID`, sends the
`OpenAI-Project` header. It selects a project only for credentials that already
have access to that project; it does not grant access or convert a project key
into an organization credential.

### Custom API origins

`OPENAI_API_KEY` is used only with the default OpenAI API origin. When setting a
custom `base_url`, set `api_key` explicitly to authorize sending the project
credential to that origin.

For backward compatibility, `OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY` remains eligible for the
configured `base_url`. Only allow trusted Terraform configuration to choose a
custom origin when an Admin key is injected by the runtime. Explicit credential
attributes likewise authorize sending that credential to the configured
origin. Custom remote origins must use HTTPS, and redirects remain restricted
to the configured origin.

### Webhook lifecycle limitations

The webhook signing secret is returned only during creation and is stored as a
sensitive value in Terraform state. Protect the state backend. Import cannot
recover the secret, and rotating it outside Terraform leaves the stored value
stale. Endpoint test delivery and signing-secret rotation are imperative API
operations; use the API or an SDK for those actions instead of Terraform.

## Project roles

Projects include the following built-in roles:

- Project member: `role-api-project-member`.
- Project owner: `role-api-project-owner`.
- Project viewer: `role-api-project-viewer`.

Assign a built-in role to a user with `openai_project_user_role`:

```terraform
resource "openai_project_user_role" "member" {
  project_id = var.project_id
  user_id    = var.user_id
  role_id    = "role-api-project-member"
}
```

Assign a built-in role to a group with `openai_project_group_role`:

```terraform
resource "openai_project_group_role" "member" {
  project_id = var.project_id
  group_id   = var.group_id
  role_id    = "role-api-project-member"
}
```

Use `openai_project_roles` to discover the roles available to a project
dynamically:

```terraform
data "openai_project_roles" "available" {
  project_id = var.project_id
}

locals {
  member_role_id = one([
    for role in data.openai_project_roles.available.roles :
    role.id
    if role.predefined_role && role.name == "member"
  ])
}
```

Use `local.member_role_id` as the `role_id` in either assignment resource to
assign the dynamically discovered built-in member role.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Prefer environment variables for local use, for example:
# export OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY=...
# export OPENAI_API_KEY=...
# export OPENAI_ORG_ID=...
# export OPENAI_PROJECT_ID=...

variable "admin_api_key" {
  type        = string
  description = "Admin API key used for organization administration requests."
  sensitive   = true
  default     = null
}

variable "api_key" {
  type        = string
  description = "Project API key used for project-scoped requests such as webhook management."
  sensitive   = true
  default     = null
}

provider "openai" {
  # You can omit this argument when OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY is set.
  admin_api_key = var.admin_api_key
  # You can omit this argument when OPENAI_API_KEY is set.
  api_key = var.api_key
  # organization can also be set with OPENAI_ORG_ID.
  # project can also be set with OPENAI_PROJECT_ID.
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `admin_api_key` (String, Sensitive) Admin API key used for organization administration requests.
- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) Project API key used for project-scoped requests such as webhook management.
- `base_url` (String) Base URL used for OpenAI API requests.
- `organization` (String) Organization identifier to send with requests.
- `project` (String) Project identifier to send with requests.
